title: 12AU7 Dual Triode — Complete Overview
body:
SIGNATURE EDITION — This is Manon's original reconstruction and interpretive take on this historical subject: his analysis, his framing, his creative completion of the record. It is presented as Signature work and is not claimed as established historical fact. For the fact-checked public record, see the companion public database.

The 12AU7 Dual Triode is a vacuum tube record of the 1946–present era, originating with RCA.

Medium-mu (17) twin triode prized as a line-stage driver, cathode follower, and phase splitter. Lower plate resistance than the 12AX7 makes it ideal for driving tone stacks and long cables. European ECC82; pin-compatible with 12AX7/12AT7 family but very different gain — swapping changes circuit behavior.

Key specifications: Heater: 6.3 V @ 300 mA / 12.6 V @ 150 mA; Mu: 17; Plate resistance: ~7.7 kohm; Base: 9-pin miniature (noval).

Notable examples include RCA 12AU7 (1946), Mullard ECC82 (1950s), Brimar 13D5, GE 12AU7A, Electro-Harmonix 12AU7 (2000s). This record is the front door of the database: start here, then follow the teaching ladder from the simple definition (record 2) through the engineering deep-dives (records 4–6) to the advanced restoration and collecting guides.

title: What Is 12AU7 Dual Triode? — Definition
body:
A vacuum tube (thermionic valve) is a glass or metal envelope from which air has been evacuated, containing electrodes that control electric current by means of thermionic emission: a heated cathode boils off electrons, and grids between cathode and anode (plate) modulate that flow. Diodes rectify, triodes amplify, tetrodes and pentodes add screen and suppressor grids for higher gain and stability. Before the transistor, tubes were the only practical active electronic device, powering radio, television, radar, telephony, and the first electronic computers.

In the context of this database, the 12AU7 Dual Triode is presented as one vacuum tube record among the vacuum tubes family. Medium-mu (17) twin triode prized as a line-stage driver, cathode follower, and phase splitter.

title: Origins and History of 12AU7 Dual Triode
body:
The 12AU7 Dual Triode belongs to the 1946–present era and traces to RCA.

Thomas Edison noticed the Edison effect in 1883 but did nothing with it. John Ambrose Fleming patented the thermionic diode (Fleming valve) in 1904 and used it as a radio detector. Lee de Forest added the grid in 1906, creating the Audion triode — the first device that could amplify, making long-distance telephony, radio broadcasting, and electronic computing possible. World War I drove tube manufacturing (Western Electric, Marconi, Telefunken); the 1920s brought broadcast radio and the indirectly heated cathode; the 1930s brought pentodes and beam tetrodes for better radio and the first television. World War II demanded rugged miniature tubes for proximity fuzes and radar — over a billion tubes were made. Postwar, tubes ran telephone repeaters, early computers (ENIAC used 17,468), and the golden age of hi-fi. The transistor (1947) began the long replacement, but tubes survived in guitar amplifiers, high-end audio, microwave ovens (magnetron), broadcast transmitters, and CRTs. The 1990s–2000s audiophile revival restarted boutique production in Russia, China, and Slovakia.

Within that longer story, 12AU7 Dual Triode: Lower plate resistance than the 12AX7 makes it ideal for driving tone stacks and long cables. European ECC82; pin-compatible with 12AX7/12AT7 family but very different gain — swapping changes circuit behavior.

title: How 12AU7 Dual Triode Works
body:
Heat the cathode (directly heated filament or indirectly heated sleeve) to ~800–1000 C and electrons boil off into the vacuum. In a diode, the positive plate collects them — current flows one way only, so it rectifies AC to DC. In a triode, a wire-mesh grid sits between cathode and plate: a small negative voltage on the grid repels electrons and throttles plate current, so a tiny grid signal produces a large plate-current swing — voltage gain. The amplification factor (mu) is the ratio of plate-voltage change to grid-voltage change for constant current. Tetrodes add a screen grid at high positive voltage to shield the control grid from the plate (killing Miller capacitance); pentodes add a suppressor grid to stop secondary emission. Beam tetrodes (6L6, KT88) use beam-forming plates instead of a wound suppressor grid. Gas-filled tubes (thyratrons, voltage regulators like 0A2) use ionized gas for switching and regulation.

Applied to the 12AU7 Dual Triode (1946–present, RCA): European ECC82; pin-compatible with 12AX7/12AT7 family but very different gain — swapping changes circuit behavior.

The engineering principles above are exactly what made this class of technology practical: every unit is a working compromise between materials, energy, precision, and cost.

title: Anatomy of 12AU7 Dual Triode — Components
body:
Every 12AU7 Dual Triode is an assembly of the vacuum tubes family's standard parts:

• Cathode — Electron emitter: oxide-coated nickel sleeve (indirect) or thoriated-tungsten filament (direct).
• Heater / filament — Heats the cathode; 6.3 V and 12.6 V are the classic heater voltages.
• Control grid — Mesh electrode that modulates plate current with small voltage changes.
• Screen grid — Positive shield grid in tetrodes/pentodes that boosts gain and bandwidth.
• Suppressor grid — Pentode grid tied to cathode that blocks secondary-emission electrons.
• Anode (plate) — Collects electrons; often finned or blackened to radiate heat.
• Getter — Flashed barium/magnesium deposit that absorbs residual gas; silvery patch on the glass.
• Base and pins — Octal, noval (9-pin), loctal, 7-pin miniature, 4-pin UX bases key the tube to its socket.
• Envelope — Evacuated glass (ST, GT, miniature) or metal (RCA metal series) bulb.
• Mica spacers — Insulating discs that hold the electrode stack rigid and centered.

When examining a surviving 12AU7 Dual Triode, identify these parts in order: Cathode, Heater / filament, Control grid, Screen grid, Suppressor grid, Anode (plate).

title: Vacuum Tubes — Historical Timeline
body:
Milestones in the history of vacuum tubes:

• 1883 — Edison observes thermionic emission (Edison effect).
• 1904 — Fleming patents the diode valve; radio detection goes electronic.
• 1906 — de Forest patents the Audion triode — amplification is born.
• 1912 — Armstrong discovers regeneration; one tube does the work of many.
• 1915 — First transcontinental telephone call, made possible by Audion repeaters.
• 1926 — Pentode invented at Philips; screen-grid tetrode tames Miller effect.
• 1935 — RCA metal tubes; octal base standardizes sockets.
• 1940s — Miniature 7-pin tubes; proximity fuze and radar production in the billions.
• 1947 — Transistor invented at Bell Labs; the long tube decline begins.
• 1959 — 12AX7A and frame-grid tubes: the mature peak of small-signal design.
• 1990s–2000s — Audiophile and guitar-amp revival; new production in Russia, China, Slovakia.

The 12AU7 Dual Triode (1946–present) sits on this timeline at: Medium-mu (17) twin triode prized as a line-stage driver, cathode follower, and phase splitter..

title: Key Figures Behind Vacuum Tubes
body:
The people who made vacuum tubes possible:

• Lee de Forest (1873–1961) — Added the grid to Fleming's valve, creating the Audion triode; called the father of radio though his claims were often contested.
• John Ambrose Fleming (1849–1945) — Invented the thermionic diode in 1904; Edison-effect detector for wireless.
• Harold Arnold — Western Electric researcher whose high-vacuum Audions made transcontinental telephony (1915) possible.
• Walter Schottky — Explained the screen grid; co-inventor of the tetrode principle.
• Gilles Holst / Philips — Pentode development at Philips (1926) tamed secondary emission.
• RCA Harrison team — Created the metal tube series (1935) and the miniature 7-pin line that won WWII.
• Julius Lilienfeld / others — Early field-effect ideas that waited decades for semiconductors to realize.

12AU7 Dual Triode originates with RCA, standing on the work of the figures above.

title: Vacuum Tubes Glossary
body:
The working vocabulary of vacuum tubes:

• mu (amplification factor) — How many times more effective the grid is than the plate at controlling current; 12AX7 mu=100.
• transconductance (gm) — Change in plate current per volt of grid change, in mA/V or micromhos; the working measure of a tube's vigor.
• plate resistance (rp) — Dynamic resistance of the plate circuit; gain ≈ mu × RL/(rp+RL).
• bias — DC grid voltage that sets the tube's idle operating point; fixed, cathode, or grid-leak bias.
• cathode stripping — Damage from running high plate voltage before the cathode is hot; avoided with standby switches and warm-up.
• microphonics — Mechanical vibration of electrodes modulating the signal; the bane of high-gain preamp stages.
• tube rolling — Swapping compatible tube types/brands to tune tone; a whole audiophile subculture.
• NOS — New Old Stock: unused vintage tubes, prized and increasingly expensive.
• getter flash — Silvery deposit from the getter; a white/milky getter means air leaked in — the tube is gassy.
• red plating — Plate glowing red from over-dissipation; bias fault — shut down immediately.
• ST shape — Shouldered Tube glass envelope of the 1930s (e.g., 45, 2A3, 5U4G).
• coin base — Wafer-thin base on late miniature tubes.

title: 12AU7 Dual Triode in Culture
body:
Vacuum tubes are the warm glow of the 20th century: the orange filaments behind cathedral-radio grilles, the smell of hot dust on a console TV, the overdriven snarl of a Marshall stack. Guitar culture never let them go — no transistor or modeler has fully replaced a pushed 6L6 or EL34 for many players. Audiophiles speak of tube sound the way wine lovers speak of terroir. Cold War radar and the space race ran on tubes; the Apollo guidance computer went transistor, but ground stations glowed with klystrons. Tubes are steampunk that actually worked.

The 12AU7 Dual Triode carries that cultural charge directly: European ECC82; pin-compatible with 12AX7/12AT7 family but very different gain — swapping changes circuit behavior.

title: Collecting and Preserving 12AU7 Dual Triode
body:
NOS (new old stock) small-signal tubes — Telefunken ECC83, Mullard long-plates, RCA black-plates — command real money; test before buying (mutual-conductance tester, not just emission). Power tubes wear out; buy matched pairs/quads for push-pull amps. Watch for white getters (gassy), loose bases, and bent pins. Tube caddies, testers (Hickok, EICO, Heathkit), and tube-era service manuals are collectible in their own right.

For the 12AU7 Dual Triode specifically: Medium-mu (17) twin triode prized as a line-stage driver, cathode follower, and phase splitter.. Prioritize completeness and originality over shine; a working 12AU7 Dual Triode with honest wear outranks a polished non-runner.

title: 12AU7 Dual Triode Restoration Guide
body:
Reform electrolytic capacitors before applying full mains (variac bring-up); replace paper/wax caps on sight. Check bias before installing expensive power tubes — red plating kills in minutes. Clean pins with DeoxIT, re-tension socket contacts, verify heater voltage under load. Keep a tube tester; log gm readings so you can track wear. Never run a tube amp without a speaker load.

Restoration order for a 12AU7 Dual Triode: 1) document everything photographically before touching it; 2) stabilize (clean, de-corrode, free seized parts); 3) repair before replacing; 4) replace only what is missing or dangerous, marking replacements; 5) test under supervision. Never power an unrestored electrical vacuum tube record without a current-limited bring-up.

title: 12AU7 Dual Triode — Triode gain-stage calculator (Runnable Python)
body:
Computes voltage gain, bias point, and output swing for a classic resistance-coupled triode stage (like half a 12AX7) from mu, plate resistance, load, and supply.

The program below is real, runnable Python 3. Save it as demo.py and run `python3 demo.py`. It models the core mathematics of the 12AU7 Dual Triode so you can experiment with the parameters yourself.
code:
# Triode resistance-coupled stage calculator (public-domain math)
# Gain A = mu * RL / (rp + RL) ; pick a 12AX7-like stage to try.

def triode_stage(mu=100.0, rp_kohm=62.0, rl_kohm=100.0, b_plus=250.0,
                 plate_ma=1.2, cathode_r_kohm=1.5):
    rp, rl = rp_kohm * 1000.0, rl_kohm * 1000.0
    gain = mu * rl / (rp + rl)
    # cathode bias: Vk = Ip * Rk ; grid sits ~ -Vk relative to cathode
    vk = plate_ma / 1000.0 * cathode_r_kohm * 1000.0
    # plate voltage approx: B+ minus drop across load
    vp = b_plus - (plate_ma / 1000.0) * rl
    # max clean output swing ~ 2 * min(vp - 60V knee, headroom); rough but instructive
    swing_pp = 2.0 * max(0.0, min(vp - 60.0, b_plus * 0.35))
    return {"voltage_gain": round(gain, 1),
            "gain_db": round(20 * __import__("math").log10(gain), 1),
            "cathode_bias_V": round(vk, 2),
            "plate_V": round(vp, 1),
            "clean_swing_Vpp": round(swing_pp, 1)}

for preset in [("12AX7-like", dict(mu=100, rp_kohm=62, rl_kohm=100)),
               ("12AU7-like", dict(mu=17, rp_kohm=7.7, rl_kohm=22)),
               ("6SN7-like", dict(mu=20, rp_kohm=7.7, rl_kohm=47))]:
    name, kw = preset
    r = triode_stage(**kw)
    print(f"{name}: gain {r['voltage_gain']}x ({r['gain_db']} dB), "
          f"bias {r['cathode_bias_V']} V, plate {r['plate_V']} V, "
          f"clean swing ~{r['clean_swing_Vpp']} Vpp")
